items.title: `scripts/lsp-latency.py`'s base archive carried `src/search-dict` but not kolt's gitignored `src/lucide`, so the base server analyzed a kolt with 56 `cannot find 'lucide'` errors, stopped early on every keystroke (a leaf keystroke 2.1 G against 4.4 G whole) and the seal's LSP ratios read x2..x7 — a false RED that the base rows' `errors` column exposed
items.discussion: Order 49 seal 1 (perf-95bf20a9.log, lsp-base-95bf20a9.log: errors 6/7 per base row, 0 on the tip); perf_gate.py prepare_kolt (which carries both since Order 47); the kolt memory's rule that any copy carries src/lucide + src/search-dict
items.body: `copy_untracked_inputs` copied `search-dict`/`src/search-dict` only. Fixed: the tuple gains `lucide`/`src/lucide` and the docstring says why (a broken program stops early, so a base row that reports errors is not a measurement). Lesson for the seal: read the base rows' `errors` column before the verdict; a base that reports errors on a clean kolt is a broken copy, not a regression. A pin that the harness's copy checks clean under the base compiler before the first edit would make this structural (S).
